newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: US provides $1.6 million for condoms in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: US provides $1.6 million for condoms in Cambodia.

text.p: The U.S. government has made a grant of $1.6 million to Population Services International (PSI) to expand its condom marketing program in Cambodia, officials said on Thursday.
The grant, provided through the U.S. Agency for International Development, will support PSI's efforts to sell condoms.
The programme is aimed at combatting the rapid spread in Cambodia of AIDS (Aquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome) and provide more families with access to condoms and oral contraception.
The grant brings to $4 million the amount of funding for PSI programmes in Cambodia.
In 1996, PSI sold 9.5 million condoms in Cambodia, a country of 10.5 million people.
The organisation promotes condom use through advertising, an aggressive sales force and a popular mascot dressed in a giant condom that makes appearances at public events.
The United Nations has said more than 100,000 Cambodians are infected with the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), which causes AIDS, and 30,000 are expected to die by 2000.
